text: Peirce's pragmatist theory of truth identifies the truth of a proposition with:
choices: whatever an individual finds expedient, satisfying, or beneficial to believe
the ideal outcome on which a community of inquirers would converge at the end of sustained rational inquiry
an isomorphism between the structure of the proposition and the structure of an atomic fact
its membership in the Absolute, the single all-embracing system of experience
explanation: For Peirce, truth is the ideal limit of inquiry — the belief that would survive indefinitely prolonged, rational investigation — an objective notion, since inquiry is answerable to how things are. Option 0 is closer to James's 'what works' pragmatism (and its individualist caricature); option 2 is Russell's structural correspondence; option 3 is Bradley's idealist coherence theory.
